merger_description:
Merck KGaA (**Merck**) proposes to acquire 100% of Bio-Techne Corporation (**Bio-Techne**)’s issued share capital through its wholly-owned subsidiary, EMD Holdings NewCo, Inc. (**Merger Sub**). Merck will acquire 100% of the outstanding common stock of Bio-Techne via a merger of Merger Sub with and into Bio-Techne with Bio-Techne surviving as a wholly-owned subsidiary of Merck.

Merck is a global science and technology company (listed on the Frankfurt Stock Exchange: MRK) headquartered in Germany. Merck operates through three business sectors: its larger Life Science and Healthcare segments, as well as its smaller Electronics segment. Merck’s Life Science portfolio is primarily focused on products and technologies supporting biopharmaceutical manufacturing, while also offering a broad catalogue of biology and chemistry products, including reagents, solvents, filters and everyday lab essentials as well as specialised products and services such as contract testing services, biomonitoring and diagnostic and regulated materials.

Bio-Techne is a publicly traded life sciences company (NASDAQ: TECH) headquartered in the United States, which specialises in reagents, analytical instruments, and precision diagnostics, supplying to academic researchers, biopharmaceutical companies, and clinical labs, among others.

Both parties supply life science analytical instruments, protein analysis techniques, bioactive small molecules, antibodies, cell culture products and other consumables.

determination_table_content.details:
When making a determination in Phase 1, the Australian Competition
and Consumer Commission (ACCC) undertakes a competition
assessment and considers whether it is appropriate for an
acquisition to be approved or subject to further assessment in
Phase 2 in accordance with section 51ABZJ of the Competition and
Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) (the Act). In doing so, the ACCC must have
regard to the object of the Act and all relevant matters, including the
interests of consumers.
For more information about the ACCC’s approach to considering
notified acquisitions, see the ACCC’s merger assessment guidelines
and interim merger process guidelines.
In conducting its competition assessment, the ACCC has considered
the information and documents that were submitted with the
notification form, information from third parties, and publicly
available information.
The ACCC has determined that the Acquisition may be put into
effect as it considers that the Acquisition would be unlikely to have
the effect of substantially lessening competition in any market. In
reaching its decision, and based on the material before it, the ACCC
makes the following findings.
In all relevant overlap products, the merged firm would continue to
face competition from alternative suppliers of life science products
globally. This includes significant global providers Thermo Fisher
Scientific and Danaher, in the case of some products, as well as
alternative suppliers that specialise in narrower sets of life science
products.
Some market participants expressed concern that Merck and Bio-
Techne were particularly close competitors in the supply of certain
products, particularly antibodies and cell culture reagents. However,
market feedback, including from Australian customers, consistently
identified alternative suppliers of all relevant product types in which
the merger parties overlap. Market feedback identified Thermo
Fisher Scientific as a particularly strong alternative supplier across a
broad range of life science products.
